---
title: "Contract with the Python package"
---

ggpclient and the Python package [ggp-client](https://jossl95.github.io/ggp_client/) are two implementations of one
contract: a file written by one is read by the other. The contract is on
[the Python site](https://jossl95.github.io/ggp_client/contract.html); in short:

- the same catalogue (`catalogue.sqlite`) and login (`.session.json`);
- the same folders and lower-case file names under `download/{raw, processed, consolidated}`;
- the same `ggp_*` provenance columns and the same `meta.json` format;
- the same rules: country-specific variables left out (the file's own `country` variable first, then a table), labels
  harmonized with one vote per country, the type that holds all for a column that differs between countries.

## How it is kept true

- `tests/testthat/fixtures` is a copy of the Python package's `tests/fixtures`: portal pages, an FFS dataset, a label
  case, and the results both must give. `test-contract.R` checks this package against them; the CI compares the copy
  with the Python repository, so the two cannot drift.
- `test-equivalence.R` runs both packages on the same downloads (the Python one through reticulate) and compares the
  data and the labels. On the 69 GGS files of both rounds the two gave the same rows, columns and labels.

## Where R differs

| | Python | R |
|---|---|---|
| numbers in a text column | `"2.0"` | `"2.0"` (the same since DuckDB stacks) or `"2"` for waves stacked with arrow |
| datetimes | no time zone | UTC |
| trailing spaces in Stata strings | kept | trimmed (haven) |
| Stata text over 2,045 characters | cut | written whole |
| readers | polars or pandas | data frames, haven labelled columns, arrow datasets |

Use the Python package when you need the command line, pandas or polars; use this one when you work in R and do not
want Python.
